def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product:
## Definition

Fix a spatial dimension $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, side length $L>0$, and odd integer $N\ge3$. Put $h=L/N$ and $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$. The periodic grid has index set $J_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ and nodes $x_j=hj$ modulo $L$. A grid scalar is a real array $u=(u_j)_{j\in J_N}$; a grid vector has $d$ real components at each node. Define
$$ \langle u,v\rangle_h=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_jv_j,\qquad \|u\|_h=\langle u,u\rangle_h^{1/2},\qquad \bar u=L^{-d}h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_j . $$ The same pairing is componentwise for grid vectors. For the coordinate vector $e_a$, define the centered field difference and positive periodic Poisson stencil by $$ (D_a^0u)_j=\frac{u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{2h},\qquad (A_hu)_j=\sum_{a=1}^d\frac{2u_j-u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{h^2}. $$
All indices wrap modulo $N$. The discrete Fourier index set is $\mathcal K_N=\{-\frac{N-1}{2},\ldots,\frac{N-1}{2}\}^d$; the character at $k\in\mathcal K_N$ is $j\mapsto e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$. This odd-grid convention has no Nyquist mode.
lem-periodic-composite-trapezoid-error:
## Statement

Let $L>0$, odd $N\ge3$, $h=L/N$, and $f\in C^2(\mathbb T_L^d)$ for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$. With the uniform tensor grid $x_j=hj$ and indices taken modulo $N$,
$$ \left|h^d\sum_{j\in(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d}f(x_j)-\int_{[0,L]^d}f(x)\,dx\right| \le \frac{L^dh^2}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_{aa}f\|_\infty . $$
def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-ga:
## Definition

On the torus and grid of [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]], an algebraic assignment shape is any family of functions $w_j:\mathbb T_L^d\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\sum_{j\in J_N}w_j(x)=1$ for every $x$. For the smooth fixed-$\varepsilon$ branch used in the force-error and ODE results, put $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/L}$ and choose the explicit even periodic kernel
$$ \eta_\varepsilon(x)=L^{-d}\prod_{a=1}^d \frac{1-\alpha_\varepsilon^2}{1-2\alpha_\varepsilon\cos(2\pi x_a/L)+\alpha_\varepsilon^2}. $$ For this smooth branch and each $x\in\mathbb T_L^d$, set $$ Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x),\qquad w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)=\frac{h^d\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x)}{Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)}. $$ Each factor in the kernel denominator is positive, so $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)>0$ and the smooth-branch weights are well-defined. For any algebraic shape family above and finitely many particle positions $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_P)$ with charges $q_1,\ldots,q_P\in\mathbb R$, write $Q=\sum_{p=1}^Pq_p$ and define deposited charge density $$ \rho_j(X)=h^{-d}\sum_{p=1}^Pq_pw_j(X_p)-Q/L^d . $$
For any grid scalar $g$, its potential gather is $(G_Xg)_p=\sum_jw_j(X_p)g_j$. For any grid vector $E$, its field gather is defined componentwise by the same weights, $(G_XE)_p=\sum_jw_j(X_p)E_j$. On the smooth fixed-$\varepsilon$ branch, $w_j$ means the explicit family $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ above.
thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson:
## Statement

Use the grid, inner product, and operator $A_h$ of [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Then $A_h$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative, $\ker A_h$ consists exactly of constant arrays, and $\operatorname{ran}A_h=\{s:\bar s=0\}$. Consequently, for every compatible source $\bar s=0$, there is a unique solution $\phi$ of $A_h\phi=s$ with the gauge $\bar\phi=0$.

For $k\in\mathcal K_N$, the Fourier character $e_k(j)=e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$ is an eigenvector with
$$ \lambda_h(k)=\frac4{h^2}\sum_{a=1}^d\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi k_a}{N}\right). $$
Only $k=0$ has eigenvalue zero.
thm-periodic-pic-zero-mean-pseudoinverse:
## Statement

For any real grid array $s$, define its mean-zero periodic Poisson pseudoinverse by
$$ A_h^\dagger s:=\text{the unique mean-zero grid array }u\text{ such that }A_hu=s-\bar s\,\mathbf1, $$
where $\bar s=L^{-d}\langle s,\mathbf1\rangle_h$. This definition is well-defined by [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]]. It gives $A_hA_h^\dagger s=s-\bar s\mathbf1$, $A_h^\dagger\mathbf1=0$, and a linear self-adjoint map on the full finite grid space.
alg-periodic-pic-zero-mean-poisson-solve:
## Definition

Input an odd $N\ge3$ periodic grid as in [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]] and a real grid source $s$. If $\bar s\ne0$, return the status incompatible-source. Otherwise compute the finite discrete Fourier coefficients $\widehat s_k=N^{-d}\sum_js_je^{-2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$. Set $\widehat\phi_0=0$ and, for each $k\ne0$, set $\widehat\phi_k=\widehat s_k/\lambda_h(k)$ with $\lambda_h(k)$ from [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]]. Return the inverse finite Fourier transform $\phi_j=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_N}\widehat\phi_ke^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$ and status success. All arithmetic here is exact real or complex arithmetic; an implementation using floating-point FFTs requires a separate perturbation analysis.
thm-periodic-pic-charge-conservation-and:
## Statement

For positions $X_1,\ldots,X_P\in\mathbb T_L^d$ and real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_P$, define $Q=\sum_pq_p$ and an admissible algebraic assignment shape $w_j$ as in [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]]. Then
$$ h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}h^{-d}\sum_{p=1}^Pq_pw_j(X_p)=Q . $$
Consequently the neutralized source $\rho_j(X)=h^{-d}\sum_pq_pw_j(X_p)-Q/L^d$ has mean zero and is in the range of the periodic Poisson operator; it therefore has a unique mean-zero potential for the gauge $\bar\phi=0$ by [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]].
thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-p:
## Statement

Let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be the explicit product kernel in [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]], with $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/L}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mu$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with mass $Q$ and total variation $\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$. Put
$$ \widehat\mu(k)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}e^{-2\pi i k\cdot y/L}\,d\mu(y),\qquad \kappa_k=2\pi k/L . $$ Then $\eta_\varepsilon$ is strictly positive, even, smooth, and has integral one. The regularized neutralized source $$ \rho_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(x-y)\,d\mu(y)-Q/L^d $$ is $C^\infty$ with zero mean. Its unique zero-mean periodic solution of $-\Delta\phi_\varepsilon^\mu=\rho_\varepsilon^\mu$ is the absolutely and uniformly differentiable Fourier series $$ \phi_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=L^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}} \frac{\left(\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{|k_a|}\right)\widehat\mu(k)} {|\kappa_k|^2}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}. $$
For every integer $r\ge0$, all spatial derivative series of order at most $r$ converge absolutely and uniformly; their bounds may depend on $r,\varepsilon,L,\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$.
lem-periodic-pic-smooth-assignment-weigh:
## Statement

For fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and periodic grid, the smooth-branch weights $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$. For every multi-index $\beta$, $\max_j\|\partial^\beta w_j^{\varepsilon,h}\|_\infty<\infty$. They are nonnegative and sum to one at every point.
thm-periodic-pic-deposition-potential-ga:
## Statement

Let $\rho^+_j=h^{-d}\sum_pq_pw_j(X_p)$ be the deposited density before background subtraction for an admissible algebraic shape $w_j$ of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]], and let $G_X$ be its scalar potential gather. For every grid scalar $\phi$,
$$ \langle\rho^+,\phi\rangle_h=\sum_{p=1}^P q_p(G_X\phi)_p . $$ For the neutralized density $\rho=\rho^+-Q/L^d$ the corresponding identity is $$ \langle\rho,\phi\rangle_h=\sum_pq_p(G_X\phi)_p-Q\bar\phi . $$
Thus the background term vanishes in the zero-mean potential gauge.
thm-periodic-pic-poisson-residual-to-gat:
## Statement

Let $s$ be a zero-mean grid source and let $\phi$ be the zero-mean solution of $A_h\phi=s$. Let $\widetilde\phi$ be any approximate grid potential, and set $r=s-A_h\widetilde\phi$; then $\bar r=0$. Define
$$ \gamma_{N,L}= \max_{\substack{k\in\mathcal K_N\\k\ne0}} \frac{\left(\sum_{a=1}^d h^{-2}\sin^2(2\pi k_a/N)\right)^{1/2}} {4h^{-2}\sum_{a=1}^d\sin^2(\pi k_a/N)} . $$ For the centered field operator $D^0=(D_a^0)_{a=1}^d$, $$ \|D^0(\phi-\widetilde\phi)\|_h\le\gamma_{N,L}\|r\|_h,\qquad \gamma_{N,L}\le\frac{h}{2\sin(\pi/N)}\le\frac L4 . $$ For any particle location $x_p$ and charge-to-mass ratio $q_p/m_p$ with $m_p>0$, the force gather using the weights of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] obeys $$ \left|\frac{q_p}{m_p}G_{x_p}\!\left(-D^0\phi+D^0\widetilde\phi\right)\right| \le\frac{|q_p|}{m_p}h^{-d/2}\gamma_{N,L}\|r\|_h . $$
Thus the norm in the force certificate is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm; the explicit $h^{-d/2}$ conversion is retained when passing from grid $L^2$ to a particle gather.
def-periodic-pic-regularized-grid-intera:
## Definition

Fix $\varepsilon>0$, $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, and a regularized one-species model with total charge $Q$ and total mass $M>0$. Let $c=Q/M$. For each position $y\in\mathbb T_L^d$, define the continuous unit-source field by taking the zero-mean solution $\phi_\varepsilon^y$ from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]] for $\mu=\delta_y$, and setting
$$ \mathcal E_\varepsilon(x,y)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(z-x)(-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon^y(z))\,dz =\frac1{L^d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}} \frac{-i\kappa_k}{|\kappa_k|^2} \left(\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{2|k_a|}\right)e^{i\kappa_k\cdot(x-y)} . $$ The series converges absolutely with all derivatives by geometric summability. For the grid branch, let $\phi_h^y$ be the mean-zero solution of $$ A_h\phi_h^y=h^{-d}w^{\varepsilon,h}(y)-L^{-d}\mathbf1 $$ whose compatibility follows from [[thm-periodic-pic-charge-conservation-and-neutralized-source]], and put $$ \mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(x,y)=\sum_{j\in J_N}w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)(-D^0\phi_h^y)_j . $$ If $z=(x,v)$ and $z'=(y,w)$ are lifted phase-space states in $\mathbb R^{2d}$, the continuum and grid mean-field kernels are $$ \mathbb K_\varepsilon(z,z')=(v,cQ\,\mathcal E_\varepsilon(x,y)),\qquad \mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z,z')=(v,cQ\,\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(x,y)). $$
The spatial components are periodic in their position variables. A finite equal-weight system $\dot z_p=P^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^P\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z_p,z_r)$ uses particle charge $Q/P$ and mass $M/P$. No claim about the limit $\varepsilon\to0$ is part of this definition.
lem-periodic-pic-shape-partition-and-qua:
## Statement

Let $d,L,N,h,\eta_\varepsilon,Z_{\varepsilon,h}$, and $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ have the meanings in [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]] and [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]]. For a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on the torus, write $\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}=|\mu|(\mathbb T_L^d)$ and define
$$ (P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j=h^{-d}\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)\,d\mu(x). $$ Put $$ C_\eta=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_{aa}\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\qquad Z_{\min}=L^d\min_{x\in\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(x)>0 . $$ Then $\sum_jw_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)=1$ for every $x$, and $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)\ge Z_{\min}$. The measure assignment satisfies $$ \left|(P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j-(\eta_\varepsilon*\mu)(x_j)\right| \le \frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}h^2 . $$ For $g\in C^2(\mathbb T_L^d)$ define $$ C_{\eta,g}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \|\partial_{aa}(\eta_\varepsilon g)\|_\infty . $$ The gathered nodal samples satisfy the explicit bound $$ \left|\sum_jw_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)g(x_j)-(\eta_\varepsilon*g)(x)\right| \le \frac{C_{\eta,g}+C_\eta\|g\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}h^2 \qquad(x\in\mathbb T_L^d). $$
thm-periodic-pic-poisson-solver-returns-:
## Statement

For every real zero-mean source $s$ on the grid of [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]], [[alg-periodic-pic-zero-mean-poisson-solver]] terminates and returns the unique $\phi$ satisfying $A_h\phi=s$ and $\bar\phi=0$. Its incompatible-source branch is taken exactly when the equation has no solution.
alg-periodic-pic-classical-rk4-step:
## Definition

Input an odd periodic grid with $N\ge3$, a fixed $\varepsilon>0$, particle count $P\ge1$, total charge $Q$, total mass $M>0$, a state $Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_P)$ with $z_p=(X_p,V_p)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$, and step $\Delta t>0$. Use the exact-evaluation phase field of [[def-periodic-pic-regularized-grid-interaction-kernel]]:
$$ F_p(Z)=\frac1P\sum_{r=1}^P\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z_p,z_r). $$ At each of four classical RK stages, evaluate this complete field at that stage's particle positions: deposit every charge $Q/P$, subtract the neutralizing background, solve its zero-mean Poisson system with [[alg-periodic-pic-zero-mean-poisson-solver]], compute centered fields, gather, and return the position and acceleration components. With $k_1=F(Z)$, $k_2=F(Z+\frac{\Delta t}{2}k_1)$, $k_3=F(Z+\frac{\Delta t}{2}k_2)$, and $k_4=F(Z+\Delta t\,k_3)$, return $$ Z^+=Z+\frac{\Delta t}{6}(k_1+2k_2+2k_3+k_4). $$
All source systems are compatible by the charge-conservation theorem; if an input violates the stated grid, mass, or shape domain, return status invalid-input; if any exact field evaluation is unavailable, return status field-solve-failure. This procedure is in exact arithmetic. It asserts no floating-point stability or error bound.
def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-g:
## Definition

Use the smooth assignment branch of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]], real particle charges $q_p$, positive masses $m_p$, and its neutralized grid density $\rho(X)$. Let $\phi(X)=A_h^\dagger\rho(X)$ denote the unique mean-zero solution from [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]]. Define the grid potential energy
$$ U_h(X)=\frac12\langle \rho(X),A_h^\dagger\rho(X)\rangle_h =\frac12\langle\rho(X),\phi(X)\rangle_h $$ and the finite-dimensional separable Hamiltonian $$ H_h(X,p)=\frac12p^TM^{-1}p+U_h(X),\qquad M=\operatorname{diag}(m_1I_d,\ldots,m_PI_d). $$
The corresponding canonical ODE is $\dot X=M^{-1}p$, $\dot p=-\nabla_XU_h(X)$. Its force is the variational force obtained by differentiating the deposited shape in $U_h$; this definition does not identify that force with ordinary field interpolation $G_XE$.
thm-periodic-pic-grid-interaction-kernel:
## Statement

For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, odd grid size $N$, and $Q,M$ as in [[def-periodic-pic-regularized-grid-interaction-kernel]], define
$$ M_x^{\varepsilon,h}=\sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\|D_x(cQ\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h})(x,y)\|_{\rm op},\qquad M_y^{\varepsilon,h}=\sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\|D_y(cQ\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h})(x,y)\|_{\rm op} $$ and $L_{\varepsilon,h}=\max\{1,M_x^{\varepsilon,h},M_y^{\varepsilon,h}\}$. These are finite mesh- and regularization-dependent constants. The phase kernel $\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}$ is globally Lipschitz in the two-variable convention $$ |\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z,z')-\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(\widetilde z,\widetilde z')| \le L_{\varepsilon,h}\bigl(|z-\widetilde z|+|z'-\widetilde z'|\bigr). $$ The continuum kernel $\mathbb K_\varepsilon$ is also globally Lipschitz with the explicit admissible constant $$ L_\varepsilon=\max\left\{1,\frac{|cQ|}{L^d} \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}}\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{2|k_a|}\right\}. $$
thm-periodic-pic-smooth-density-grid-for:
## Statement

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with total mass $Q$. Let $\rho_\varepsilon=\eta_\varepsilon*\mu-Q/L^d$ and let $\phi_\varepsilon$ be its unique zero-mean periodic Poisson potential from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]]. Put $E_\varepsilon=-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon$. Use the shape and periodic centered-difference Poisson operator of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] and [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Let $s_h=P_h^\varepsilon\mu-Q/L^d$, let $A_h\phi_h=s_h$ with $\bar\phi_h=0$, set $E_{h,j}=-D^0\phi_h$, and gather $G_hE_h$ using the same shape. Define
$$ C_{\rm dep}=\frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV},\quad C_{\rm FD}=\frac1{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^4\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\quad C_{\rm src}=C_{\rm dep}+C_{\rm FD}, $$ where $C_\eta,Z_{\min}$ are from [[lem-periodic-pic-shape-partition-and-quadrature-bound]]. Put $$ C_3=\frac16\left(\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^3\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad C_{\rm int}=\frac{C_{\eta,E}+\|E_\varepsilon\|_\infty C_\eta}{Z_{\min}}, \quad C_{\eta,E}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \|\partial_{aa}(\eta_\varepsilon E_\varepsilon)\|_\infty . $$ Then the source $s_h$ is compatible and $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2}\left(\gamma_{N,L}C_{\rm src}+C_3\right) +C_{\rm int}h^2. $$
The displayed $\gamma_{N,L}$ is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm of [[thm-periodic-pic-poisson-residual-to-gathered-force-bound]] and satisfies $\gamma_{N,L}\le L/4$. Thus for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this fixed-$\varepsilon$ force error tends to zero as $h\to0$. Every constant depends on the stated smooth regularized solution and kernel; this is not an $\varepsilon\to0$ estimate.
thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-:
## Statement

For the Hamiltonian grid model of [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], let $\phi=A_h^\dagger\rho(X)$. Its position gradient is
$$ \nabla_{X_p}U_h(X)=q_p\sum_{j\in J_N}\nabla w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(X_p)\phi_j . $$
Along every differentiable solution of $\dot X=M^{-1}p$, $\dot p=-\nabla_XU_h(X)$, the continuous semidiscrete energy $H_h(X(t),p(t))$ is constant. This is an invariant of the exact finite-grid ODE; no time-discrete energy conservation is asserted.
thm-periodic-pic-mean-field-error-with-f:
## Statement

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and grid width $h$. Let $\mathbb K_\varepsilon$ and $\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}$ be the phase kernels of [[def-periodic-pic-regularized-grid-interaction-kernel]], and let $L_\varepsilon$ be the two-variable global Lipschitz constant of [[thm-periodic-pic-grid-interaction-kernel-is-globally-lipschitz]]. Suppose a probability characteristic solution $\mu_t$ for $\mathbb K_\varepsilon$ and an equal-weight finite-particle grid solution with empirical law $\nu_t^h$ are defined on $[0,T]$, with finite first moments and integrable path suprema. Assume the uniform grid-force defect
$$ \delta_{\varepsilon,h}=\sup_{z,z'\in\mathbb R^{2d}} |\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z,z')-\mathbb K_\varepsilon(z,z')|<\infty . $$ If $\delta_0=W_1(\nu_0^h,\mu_0)$ is the actual initial empirical-measure error, then for every $0\le t\le T$, $$ W_1(\nu_t^h,\mu_t)\le e^{2L_\varepsilon t} \left(\delta_0+t\delta_{\varepsilon,h}\right). $$
No rate for $\delta_0$ is implied: in particular, no dimension-free $P^{-1/2}$ Wasserstein rate is assumed.
thm-periodic-pic-rk4-finite-time-error-o:
## Statement

Fix $\varepsilon>0$, grid width $h$, particle count $P\ge1$, and final time $T>0$. Apply classical RK4 from [[alg-periodic-pic-classical-rk4-step]] to the autonomous finite-dimensional PIC system
$$ \dot Z=F_{\varepsilon,h}(Z),\qquad (F_{\varepsilon,h}(Z))_p=\frac1P\sum_{r=1}^P \mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z_p,z_r),\qquad z_p=(X_p,V_p). $$ Let $Z(t)$ be an exact solution on $[0,T]$. Assume $F_{\varepsilon,h}$ is $C^4$ on an open set containing a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T$; the exact path, all numerical states, and every RK4 stage generated from both the exact and numerical starting states lie in $\mathcal T$; and all derivatives of $F_{\varepsilon,h}$ through order four are bounded there. Let $h_t=T/n$ for an integer $n\ge1$, $h_t\le h_0$, and initialize exactly. Put $$ L_F=2L_{\varepsilon,h},\qquad L_*=L_Fe^{L_Fh_0}, $$ and let $C_4$ be a uniform RK4 exact-start defect constant on this tube. Then, for every grid time $t_k=kh_t\le T$, $$ \|Z_k-Z(t_k)\|_2\le \begin{cases} C_4\dfrac{e^{L_*T}-1}{L_*}h_t^4,&L_*>0,\\[4pt] C_4Th_t^4,&L_*=0. \end{cases} $$
The tube, exact-solution, and stage-admissibility hypotheses are conditional; this is a fixed-$\varepsilon$, fixed-grid finite-particle time error, not a continuum or singular-force estimate.
thm-periodic-pic-leapfrog-geometric-prop:
## Statement

Let $H_h(X,p)=\frac12p^TM^{-1}p+U_h(X)$ be [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], with $M$ symmetric positive definite and $U_h\in C^3(\mathbb R^{dP})$ periodic. Let $\Phi_{\Delta t}=K_{\Delta t/2}\circ D_{\Delta t}\circ K_{\Delta t/2}$ be the leapfrog map with the kick and drift conventions of [[def-leapfrog-step-map]]. Then:

1. For every signed step $\Delta t$, $\Phi_{\Delta t}^{-1}=\Phi_{-\Delta t}$.
2. Every step is symplectic.
3. Assuming Countable Choice, every step preserves Lebesgue volume on phase space.
4. On a finite interval $[0,T]$, if the exact and numerical paths, all kick/drift stages, and all line segments in the comparison lie in a common compact convex tube and the Hamiltonian vector field has bounded derivatives through order two there, the leapfrog trajectory error is at most $C_VTe^{LT}\Delta t^2$ for exact initialization and sufficiently small $\Delta t=T/n$.

The exact continuous flow conserves $H_h$ by [[thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-gradient-and-conserves-energy]]. No claim says the leapfrog map preserves $H_h$ exactly or that modified-energy estimates hold outside the analytic tube hypotheses of the geometric-integration suppliers.
thm-periodic-pic-staged-fixed-regulariza:
## Statement

Fix $\varepsilon>0$, grid width $h$, particle count $P$, and $T>0$. Assume the smooth fixed-regularization hypotheses of [[thm-periodic-pic-smooth-density-grid-force-consistency]], and that the translated unit-source regularized densities $\eta_\varepsilon(\cdot-y)-L^{-d}$ satisfy its derivative bounds uniformly in $y$. Let $\delta_{\varepsilon,h}$ be the uniform phase-kernel defect from [[thm-periodic-pic-mean-field-error-with-force-defect]]. The consistency theorem gives the explicit estimate
$$ \delta_{\varepsilon,h} \le |cQ|\left[ L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2}\bigl(\gamma_{N,L}C_{\rm src}^{(1)}+C_3^{(1)}\bigr) +C_{\rm int}^{(1)}h^2 \right], $$ where $C_{\rm src}^{(1)},C_3^{(1)},C_{\rm int}^{(1)}$ are the constants of that theorem evaluated at a unit point source; translation of the continuum source leaves their derivative suprema unchanged, while the shape quadrature constants are independent of the translate. Define the RK4 empirical measure by $\nu_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n)=P^{-1}\sum_{p=1}^P\delta_{z_p^{\Delta t}(t_n)}$. Put $$ \delta_0=W_1(\nu_0^h,\mu_0),\qquad C_{\rm RK}= \begin{cases} C_4(e^{L_*T}-1)/L_*,&L_*>0,\\ C_4T,&L_*=0, \end{cases} $$ using the constants of [[thm-periodic-pic-rk4-finite-time-error-on-a-controlled-tube]]. For exact initialization, a common admissible initial coupling, and the same compact-tube hypotheses, the RK4 empirical measure $\nu_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n)$ and regularized characteristic solution $\mu_\varepsilon(t_n)$ satisfy $$ W_1\!\left(\nu_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n),\mu_\varepsilon(t_n)\right) \le \frac{C_{\rm RK}}{\sqrt P}\Delta t^4 +e^{2L_\varepsilon T}\left(\delta_0+T\delta_{\varepsilon,h}\right), \qquad t_n\le T. $$
The terms are time error, prescribed initial empirical error, and fixed-$\varepsilon$ mesh-force error. No universal rate for $\delta_0$ and no $\varepsilon\to0$ singular Vlasov–Poisson limit is asserted.
ex-periodic-high-frequency-pic-sampling-:
## Statement

On $\mathbb T_{2\pi}$, take the smooth source $\rho(x)=\cos(6x)$ and solve $-\phi''=\rho$ with zero mean. Its exact electric field $E=-\phi'$ is $E(x)=\frac16\sin(6x)$. On the five-node Fourier-collocation grid $x_j=2\pi j/5$, the sampled source is exactly $\cos(x_j)$. The mean-zero collocation solution is $\phi_N(x)=\cos x$, and the computed field is $E_N(x)=\sin x$. At every grid node, $E_N(x_j)=6E(x_j)$. This is a spectral-sampling aliasing example; it is not the centered finite-difference operator defined on the main PIC page.
cex-periodic-nonneutral-source-has-no-po:
## Statement

Take the one-dimensional periodic grid with $L=1$ and odd $N\ge3$, one particle of charge $q=1$, and any nonnegative normalized assignment shape. If the deposited density $s_j=h^{-1}w_j(X)$ is sent directly to $A_h\phi=s$ without subtracting the neutralizing background $1/L$, then the equation has no solution.
ex-cold-two-stream-stipulated-pic-experi:
## Statement

Here is a fully specified cold two-stream input for the fixed-$\varepsilon$ periodic grid model. Let $d=1$, $L=2\pi$, $N=63$, $P=126$, $Q=M=1$, $\varepsilon=1/5$, and $\Delta t=10^{-3}$ with $4000$ steps to $T=4$. For $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $j\in\mathbb Z/63\mathbb Z$, assign charge and mass $1/126$ and set
$$ X_{\sigma,j}(0)=\left(\frac{2\pi j}{63}+\sigma\,\frac1{100}\cos\frac{2\pi j}{63}\right)\pmod{2\pi},\qquad V_{\sigma,j}(0)=\frac{\sigma}{2}. $$
Use the smooth assignment shape, neutralizing background, centered periodic Poisson solve, and exact-arithmetic RK4 update from the A page. The two beams are cold because each beam has one velocity value. This is a stipulated numerical experiment only: it asserts no growth rate, nonlinear saturation, or physical validation.
ex-periodic-smooth-density-poisson-grid-:
## Statement

Let $d=1$, $L=2\pi$, $a=1/2$, and let the probability measure $\mu$ have density
$$ d\mu(y)=\frac{1+a\cos y}{2\pi}\,dy. $$ For $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/(2\pi)}$, the regularized neutralized source and zero-mean field are $$ \rho_\varepsilon(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon}{2\pi}\cos x, \qquad E_\varepsilon(x)=-\phi_\varepsilon'(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon}{2\pi}\sin x. $$ The gathered continuum target is $(\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon)(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon^2}{2\pi}\sin x$. On any odd grid with spacing $h=2\pi/N$, the fixed-$\varepsilon$ theorem gives $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le (2\pi)^{1/2}h^{3/2}(\gamma_{N,2\pi}C_{\rm src}+C_3)+C_{\rm int}h^2, $$
where the constants are explicitly defined in [[thm-periodic-pic-smooth-density-grid-force-consistency]]. This tends to zero along odd $N\to\infty$ at fixed $\varepsilon$.
ex-periodic-pic-leapfrog-energy-drift-fo:
## Statement

As a scalar diagnostic, consider the separable harmonic Hamiltonian $H(q,p)=\frac12(p^2+q^2)$ and one kick-drift-kick step with $\Delta t=1/2$ from $(q_0,p_0)=(1,0)$. It returns
$$ (q_1,p_1)=\left(\frac78,-\frac{15}{32}\right),\qquad H(q_1,p_1)=\frac{1009}{2048}\ne\frac12=H(q_0,p_0). $$
The exact oscillator conserves $H$. This abstract quadratic test is not claimed to be a trajectory of the periodic electrostatic potential $U_h$ from [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]]; it shows why symplecticity or reversibility alone cannot imply exact preservation of an arbitrary Hamiltonian. On the separate PIC branch, [[thm-periodic-pic-leapfrog-geometric-properties-and-order-two-error]] proves its own reversible/symplectic and conditional order-two properties. The exact semidiscrete energy result there is [[thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-gradient-and-conserves-energy]].
